source: McDonald's technology investor presentations and corporate disclosures
interpretation_scope: McDonald's proprietary POS software. Owned and operated by McDonald's Corp. System-of-record layer for US company and franchise units. Not a third-party vendor deployment.
strategic_note: Deeply entrenched proprietary system. Replacement risk near zero without a deliberate corporate divestiture or platform shift. Relevant for vendors seeking integration access rather than displacement.

source: QSR industry hardware approvals and NCR investor references
interpretation_scope: NCR appears as an approved hardware and POS-adjacent infrastructure vendor. Not the system-of-record POS software. McDonald's owns NewPOS at the software layer. NCR role is hardware approval list or regional infrastructure.
strategic_note: Do not conflate hardware approval with POS ownership. Verify scope before asserting NCR as the McDonald's POS vendor. NewPOS is the software layer.

interpretation_scope: PAR is also an approved hardware vendor for McDonald's. This does not imply PAR owns the system-of-record POS software; NewPOS remains the system-of-record POS layer.
strategic_note: Preserve as a distinct hardware-approval edge. Useful for McDonald's hardware/service ecosystem mapping and PAR relationship relevance, not a POS displacement claim.

product: NCR and PAR equipment resale / installation / service
interpretation_scope: MAPS resells NCR and PAR equipment and retains McDonald's installation and service business. MAPS should be modeled as reseller/service coverage, not as hardware manufacturer or POS software owner.
strategic_note: This is a channel/service edge. Keep separate from NCR/PAR hardware approval and NewPOS system-of-record software.

interpretation_scope: HP is an approved hardware vendor for McDonald's internationally, but not domestically. This edge is international-only and must not be used as a US/domestic vendor claim.
strategic_note: Geography is the claim boundary. Surface HP only for international McDonald's hardware context unless corroborated domestic evidence appears.

source: PAR Technology Q3 2023 and Q4 2023 earnings calls and press releases
interpretation_scope: PAR Brink POS being actively deployed across Burger King US franchisee network. Franchisee adoption in progress. Not yet full deployment. Replacing legacy NCR/Aloha in most markets.
strategic_note: Active rollout with material penetration. PAR has disclosed BK as a flagship Brink customer. Monitor rollout completion rate and franchisee acceptance. Competitive pressure from Oracle and others.

source: QSR industry coverage of Burger King technology transition 2022-2024
interpretation_scope: NCR Aloha POS was the legacy system-of-record for significant portion of Burger King US franchisee base. Being displaced by PAR Brink rollout. Still present in markets where rollout is incomplete.
strategic_note: Legacy incumbent in active replacement. NCR relationship is declining. Useful signal for PAR penetration rate benchmarking.

source: Yum! Brands technology disclosures and trade press
interpretation_scope: NCR Aloha has been the primary POS platform for Taco Bell US locations. Yum! Brands has invested in digital integration layers on top of existing POS infrastructure.
strategic_note: Yum! Brands (TBL parent) has an ongoing digital investment agenda. Monitor for proprietary POS development or displacement signals within the Yum! ecosystem.

source: QSR industry technology coverage and Wendy's technology press
interpretation_scope: NCR Aloha POS deployed across majority of Wendy's US company and franchise locations. Legacy system-of-record. Wendy's has explored digital ordering integrations layered on top.
strategic_note: Long-running incumbent. Wendy's technology roadmap has included digital ordering investment. Watch for displacement signals from PAR or Toast as franchise tech modernization continues.

source: Oracle MICROS QSR customer references and trade press
interpretation_scope: Oracle MICROS deployed broadly across Subway US franchise network. MICROS is the system-of-record POS layer. Subway's franchise model means individual franchisee adoption can vary.
strategic_note: Entrenched Oracle MICROS deployment. Subway's distributed franchise model makes a wholesale replacement highly complex. Oracle relationship is stable.

source: Chick-fil-A technology blog and restaurant technology trade press
interpretation_scope: Chick-fil-A develops and operates proprietary technology including POS. Known for vertical integration of restaurant technology. External vendor POS is not disclosed as the system-of-record.
strategic_note: Technology independence is a strategic posture for Chick-fil-A. Vendor displacement opportunity is low. Integration partnership is the relevant opportunity.

source: Domino's investor relations and technology press — PULSE POS has been publicly disclosed
interpretation_scope: Domino's PULSE POS is a proprietary system developed and operated by Domino's corporate. Deployed across US company and franchise locations. One of the most cited examples of restaurant-owned technology in the industry.
strategic_note: Domino's is a technology-first brand. PULSE is deeply embedded. The relevant opportunity is integration (delivery middleware, loyalty, analytics) not POS displacement.

source: Chipotle technology disclosures and Oracle QSR case references
interpretation_scope: Oracle MICROS is the system-of-record POS for Chipotle US locations. Chipotle has layered digital ordering and loyalty systems on top of MICROS.
strategic_note: Stable Oracle MICROS deployment. Chipotle's digital investment is extensive but at the digital/loyalty/ordering layer rather than POS replacement. Monitor for second-line stack changes.

source: Oracle retail/hospitality case studies and Starbucks technology disclosures
interpretation_scope: Oracle MICROS widely cited as POS foundation for Starbucks US company-operated locations. Starbucks has developed extensive proprietary digital layers (app, loyalty, mobile order) on top of POS infrastructure.
strategic_note: POS layer is stable and Oracle-anchored. The strategic action is at the digital/loyalty/ordering layer where Starbucks builds proprietary. Not a displacement opportunity.

source: Restaurant technology trade press and Dunkin' franchisee technology references
interpretation_scope: Radiant Systems (now part of NCR) cited as legacy POS platform for Dunkin' locations. Dunkin' franchise model means technology adoption is franchisee-driven. Current state may vary by market.
strategic_note: Legacy POS with moderate certainty. Dunkin' franchise model means centralized replacement is difficult. Treat as lead for verification rather than confirmed current state.
